nodes.text:
1/ 📈 WWSCAN Weekly Data

Respiratory Weekly Update: SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and RSV are in the “High” category nationwide. The other respiratory viruses (Influenza B, HMPV, and EV-D68) we monitor remain in the “Low” wastewater category nationwide and not in seasonal onset. https://t.co/AhtHkzlwXu

nodes.author: RickABright
nodes.text: This is nice, I’m very supportive of the effort. However, w/o ability to ID #H5N1 in even more specific sites, overall value for flu is limited. Sequencing & subtyping of flu from wastewater is possible & affordable. Rapid/full transparency of data is essential to detect & mitigate an outbreak.

nodes.author: JN1171
nodes.text: @RickABright @WastewaterSCAN If you go into charting feature, they do offer a "Subtype" option where you can specify H5. https://t.co/KZKRRE2pmV

nodes.author: MixZA92
nodes.text: @WastewaterSCAN Will the availability of this data be impacted by Trump admin policies?

nodes.author: WastewaterSCAN
nodes.text: 2/ COVID-19: Nationwide, SARS-CoV-2 is in the “High” category with high concentrations and no significant trend up or down over the last 3 weeks. https://t.co/Dwpzh2sMWW

nodes.author: WastewaterSCAN
nodes.text: 3/ COVID-19 Variants: In sequencing data from a subset of WWSCAN sites, we are seeing the KP.3 variant in light blue (33.1%) and XEC variant in green (32.6%) make up approximately 66% of variants. Note sequencing data has a longer lag of 1-2 weeks after collection. https://t.co/6OX9FtbgSO

nodes.author: WastewaterSCAN
nodes.text: 4/ Influenza: Nationally, Flu A is in the “High” category with high concentrations and no significant trend up or down over the last 3 weeks. Flu B is in the “Low” category nationally and in all regions. https://t.co/LQkl7GoInf

nodes.author: hismerecry
nodes.text: Wow northeast flu is up sharply and high. I got flu A, a little over a month ago and it was first time I’ve had flu in 25 years. 97 year old Grandma got COVID for second time almost 3 weeks ago was hospitalized for 4 days and is recovering in nursing home still. She couldn’t walk very weak and tired and didn’t have an appetite.

nodes.author: WastewaterSCAN
nodes.text: 5/ H5 influenza marker: H5 detected in 18 states since start of monitoring - AR, CA, CO, DE, FL, IA, ID, IL, ME, MI, MN, NE, NV, NJ, SD, TN, TX, & UT. As of 1/22/24, CA, CO, IA, ID, MI, MN, NV, SD, TX & UT reported infected cattle herds. Recent wastewater detections in CA & NJ. https://t.co/IA7tZ1x3xq

nodes.author: hismerecry
nodes.text: @WastewaterSCAN Is there any detection in Connecticut?

nodes.author: WastewaterSCAN
nodes.text: 6/ RSV: RSV is in the “High” category nationally with high concentrations and a downward trend over the last 3 weeks. https://t.co/LREvuqVYjQ

nodes.author: WastewaterSCAN
nodes.text: 7/ EV-D68: EV-D68 is in the “Low” category nationally and in all regions. Levels are still elevated in the West, but few samples are positive in other regions. https://t.co/cZKJqqkMV5

nodes.author: WastewaterSCAN
nodes.text: 8/ Norovirus: Norovirus is in the “High” category nationally with high concentrations but a downward trend over the last 3 weeks. All regions remain in the “High” category. https://t.co/p5y8yMA6N2
